text: When you work with APIs, you send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most modern APIs use JSON, a simple text format that both humans and computers can read easily. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, usually by adding a key or token to your request. This proves that you have permission to access the data. However, most APIs have rate limits, which means you can only make a certain number of requests per minute or hour. If you exceed this limit, you’ll get an error. So, it’s important to handle errors properly in your code, for example by checking the response status and retrying after a short wait. Good error handling makes your application more reliable and user-friendly.
